title: Establish SLI provenance, calibration runs, and escrowed error budgets for blue-green model rollouts
creator: Ava Johnson
description: Background: As we increase model rollout cadence (blue/green and canary patterns) we need a canonical, auditable source-of-truth for all SLIs used in gating and error-budget accounting. Current practice mixes telemetry (edge-proxied latency), application-side metrics (model success/error), and downstream quality checks (promptset pass/fail) in an ad-hoc way. That ambiguity causes disagreement during rollouts and makes automated gating brittle.
objectives: Define a canonical list of endpoint-level SLIs with explicit provenance (metric source, aggregation window, and pre/post-processing),
Establish calibration run procedures to map quality SLIs (prompt set-based) to traffic-weighted service SLIs,
Introduce an "error budget escrow" mechanism to hold and allocate error budget during blue/green changes so that rollouts can consume a bounded portion without harming global SLOs,
Surface rollout-aware dashboards and alerts that show escrow usage, calibration deltas, and rollback recommendations.
proposed_sli_definitions: Availability: successful-response-rate measured at the edge ingress proxies (status 200s + valid model output) with 1m rolling windows, aggregated per-route and per-model-variant.
Latency: client-observed tail latencies (p95, p99) derived from edge tracing spans; compute trimmed mean for p95 to ignore instrumentation noise.
Quality SLI: promptset pass-rate computed by the evaluation pipeline (nightly calibration jobs) and emitted as a time-series with tags for promptset-id and model-version.
Error type SLI: fraction of responses with deterministic failure codes (model OOM, decoder error, invalid output) from the runtime logs, deduplicated per-request-id.
Resource SLI: GPU utilization and queue depth per worker as a leading indicator; converted to synthetic SLI for predictive gating.
data_provenance_rules: All SLIs must document source (edge, runtime, eval pipeline), collection interval, aggregation function, and sampling bias notes.
Edge-derived SLIs are the authoritative source for availability and latency unless explicit runtime-side invariant is declared for a route.
Quality SLIs are decoupled: they must be computed from controlled calibration runs (see calibration plan) and correlated to production traffic via the mapping job.
Telemetry ingestion must include a signed metadata block (pipeline run id, job id, sampling fraction) to support audit and backfill operations.
calibration_plan: Run nightly calibration jobs that: 1) execute canonical promptsets against candidate model-variants, 2) compute pass/fail and quality deltas relative to the incumbent, 3) estimate the expected impact on production success-rate given current traffic mix.
Produce a single calibration artifact per model-variant containing quality_sli_time_series, confidence intervals, and recommended traffic allocation for safe ramping.
Calibration jobs must run in each region where we serve to detect geo-specific quality variance.
Define a minimum sample size and statistical significance threshold (default alpha=0.05) for calibration artifacts to be considered valid gates.
error_budget_escrow_spec: At rollout start, create an escrow account for the target route that holds up to X% of the incumbent's remaining error budget (configurable, default 20%).
Escrow tokens are timeboxed and expire after the rollout window unless explicitly reclaimed.
Rollout stages (canary->ramp->cutover) can consume escrow tokens; consumption is audited and visible in the rollout dashboard.
If escrow consumption exceeds a pre-declared burn-rate threshold, automated rollback is triggered; otherwise, remaining escrow is merged back into the incumbent's error budget at stage completion.
Escrow accounting must be tenant-aware: for multi-tenant routes, ownership of escrow consumption is attributed to tenants proportionally for billing and SLA reconciliation.
rollout_gates_and_thresholds: Canary gate: 1% traffic for 60 minutes; require no >5% relative regression on quality SLI and no absolute latency p99 increase >150ms.
Ramp gate: progressive traffic doubling every 30 minutes with calibration artifact re-check at each step.
Final cutover: only permitted if cumulative escrow consumption < configured cutoff (default 50% of escrow) and no critical error-type SLI spikes.
Rollback triggers: sustained availability drop >1% absolute for 10 minutes, quality SLI regression exceeding calibrated confidence interval, or escrow burn-rate >2x planned rate.
multi_region_and_failover_interaction: Escrow accounts are region-scoped; global rollouts allocate escrow per-region proportional to regional traffic to avoid cross-region budget pollution.
When a region fails over, the regional escrow is quarantined and cannot be used by other regions until a reconciliation job runs.
Failover combined with an ongoing rollout requires rollback of the local variant unless calibration artifacts indicate cross-region compatibility.
Circuit breakers take precedence: if regional circuit breaker trips, escrowed rollouts are immediately paused and incident runbook invoked.
circuit_breaker_integration: Circuit breaker thresholds (latency, error-type SLI) are shadowed during canary to report potential trips before live traffic triggers them.
If a breaker trips during a ramp, escalate to automatic rollback and postmortem analysis; block re-rollout until cooldown and corrective action.
Expose an API to link circuit-breaker events to escrow accounting so operator consoles can correlate cost of rollouts with protective actions.
observability_and_dashboards: Rollout dashboard that shows escrow balance, consumption timeline, calibration artifact summary, and live SLI drift for incumbent vs candidate.
Per-route SLI provenance view showing raw sources (edge traces, runtime logs, calibration job ids) and last successful ingestion time.
Alert rule templates: canary-fail, escrow-overburn, calibration-stale, and region-failover-during-rollout.
Add traceable links to PRs, calibration job runs, and design docs in panel annotations.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): instrument provenance metadata for existing SLI pipelines and run calibration jobs for top 20 high-traffic routes.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement escrow ledger prototype and integrate with the rollout controller; test in staging with synthetic traffic.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): enable rollout gating by default for blue/green flows on selected non-critical routes; collect metrics and retro.
Phase 4: extend to multi-region rollouts and tenant-aware escrow accounting; update runbooks and train on-call teams.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Calibration artifacts are noisy for low-volume routes. Mitigation: enforce minimum sample size and use longer calibration windows or synthetic augmentation.
Risk: Escrow complexity leads to operator confusion. Mitigation: provide clear defaults, readable dashboards, and a single-click abort on rollout console.
Risk: Region-specific quality deltas cause rollout divergence. Mitigation: block global cutover until per-region calibration passes and require region-by-region cutover policy.
open_questions: What default escrow percentage should be used for different route criticalities (P0/P1/P2)?
How do we bill escrow consumption back to tenants when using shared pools?
Should we incorporate canary shadowing and traffic-splitting for quality evaluation rather than relying only on calibration artifacts?
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI schema and provenance metadata is adopted by edge, runtime, and eval pipelines with automated validation checks.
Nightly calibration jobs produce artifacts for >80% of top-50 routes and are visible in the rollout dashboard.
Escrow ledger prototype supports create/consume/expire flows and is wired into the rollout controller for staging rollouts.
At least one blue/green rollout in staging uses escrow and completes without manual intervention, with full audit trail.
tasks: Instrument provenance fields in telemetry ingestion (edge & runtime).
Implement calibration job runner and artifact storage (include regional runs).
Design and implement escrow ledger API and lightweight UI components for dashboarding.
Add rollout controller hooks for escrow checks and rollback automation.
Create alert templates and dashboard panels; run firefighting tabletop exercise.
Document runbook and host training session for on-call and release engineers.
